evidence.note: Extensive upfront study of all three test suites, including wacc's feature-ordered chapters and c-testsuite tags/sizes, followed by an initial TodoWrite plan — shows awareness of the feature landscape and rough sequencing.

Wrote the entire pipeline (lexer/pp/types/ast/parser/sema/codegen) upfront before any compile. Foundational representation (types, symbol tables) preceded dependent codegen, but this is pipeline-stage decomposition rather than per-feature milestones with explicit done-signals.
Staged bring-up: got simplest programs compiling/running (basic compile, printf) before layering more features — matches the 'get simplest programs compiling then layer' behavior of anchor 5.

Dominant mode is a reactive test-failure loop: run suite, list failures, pick next failing test, diagnose, fix, re-run. Completion is checked per-test and via periodic full-suite tallies, but ordering is driven by whatever fails next, not an explicit dependency-ordered milestone plan.
Periodic TodoWrite checkpoints provide coarse milestone/progress tracking across the horizon, but content-level milestone definitions with named certifying tests are not evidenced.

reasoning: The agent oriented well and worked in sensible stages — study the suites, build the pipeline, get the simplest programs compiling, then layer features while checking against test subsets — which squarely matches anchor 5. It does not reach anchor 8: there is no explicit dependency-ordered milestone plan pairing each feature with its required pipeline changes and specific certifying tests; instead the long tail is reactive, failure-by-failure iteration. It sits above 3 because completion criteria (specific tests passing plus full-suite tallies) are consistently applied at each stage.
